How to read this dashboard / sources & method

Start with sectors beating SPY, then check whether their relative momentum is improving. A sector can fall in price while outperforming a falling market. Advancing counts sectors with positive returns; outperforming counts sectors beating SPY. Neither measures breadth within each sector.

1M uses the last completed US calendar month versus the preceding month: on November 1, October versus September. Each month uses the previous month’s final trading close as its baseline. 3M uses the last three completed calendar months versus the preceding three. 1D and 1W use 1 and 5 common trading sessions versus the preceding equal-length block. YTD starts at the preceding year’s last close and compares with the same number of sessions in the prior year. Calendar months follow the New York date. The ranking shows previous and current periods in separate columns with the same magnitude scale; color and signed labels distinguish gains from losses. Rotation change shows current minus previous in percentage points and rank movement. Sort by current, previous, rotation change or rank improvement. Missing comparisons show a dash. Adjusted closes include the provider’s split and dividend adjustments. Daily candles still in progress are excluded, with a 15-minute buffer after the regular session ends. All sectors and SPY share common dates. The stock sample uses these same endpoints; missing endpoints stay unavailable.

The rotation chart uses a fixed 21-session relative-return spread and its five-session change, independent of the selected return period. This is a simple descriptive model, not a standardized RRG indicator or a forecast. No ETF creations/redemptions, investor transactions, fund flows or within-sector breadth are available here.

The server caches complete snapshots for 30 minutes, retries failures after 30 minutes and retains a labelled last-good snapshot for at most seven days. Refresh respects that cache. Check the session date, especially around US holidays. No API key is required.
